about: The model's tools. The server offers the enabled ones to the model; the browser runs them. One source for both: a contract test checks that the browser runs exactly the enabled tools. A tool is enabled once the browser can run it.
guidance: Use your tools whenever data, calculation or a visual would make the answer better. Look at the data before you draw conclusions, and check your own output when a tool reports back.

tools.name: run_js
tools.description: Run JavaScript (top-level await allowed) in the user's browser, in a locked sandbox with no network. Available: fs.readdir() lists the files you can use (for now three demo files: demo/sales.csv and demo/sales.xlsx with the same 2,000 sales, and demo/report.pdf, a sales report); fs.readFile(name) gives a CSV or other text file as a string and an Excel file as a Uint8Array (files up to 1 MB; not PDFs); sql(query) runs DuckDB SQL over the CSV and Excel files, e.g. SELECT * FROM read_csv('demo/sales.csv') or read_xlsx('demo/sales.xlsx'), and resolves to an array of row objects (dates as ISO text); pdf.html(name) reads a PDF (up to 1 MB) and resolves to {html, notes}: the PDF as HTML, one div with data-page per page, blocks with data-bbox, tables as <table>, and text hidden on the page (data-hidden) kept as elements without their text (the OCR text of a scanned page stays); parse it with new DOMParser().parseFromString(html, "text/html") and querySelectorAll (table.querySelectorAll("tr"), row.querySelectorAll("td, th"): there is no table.rows or row.cells); d3 is loaded, and document is a small virtual page, so ordinary d3 code builds SVG: return svg.node() and the user sees the chart. You get back JSON with the returned value, console.log output and any error; when a PDF had hidden text, its "hidden" field names the file and how many hidden texts were kept from you: the user can look at them below the call and add them to their message, so point them there if they ask. Each call has 30 seconds and starts fresh: nothing carries over between calls. The whole result is cut to 50,000 characters, so return summaries and extracts, not whole tables or whole HTML.

tools.name: render_html
tools.description: Show the user a page you wrote: a whole HTML document or a fragment, with its scripts running and d3 available. There is no network. You get back any errors and a short summary of what appeared, so you can check your work.

tools.name: fetch_url
tools.description: Fetch a web page or file and get it back as readable text. The user may be asked to approve the request first.
